newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power flat amid cool weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power flat amid cool weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast ended mostly flat Thursday against Wednesday's levels amid cool weather in much of the region, market sources said.
Modest daily power demand mitigated concerns over reduced generating capability due to plant outages in the northeastern corner of the U.S., traders said.
New York Power Authority's 800 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear plant in Scriba, N.Y., was still operating at reduced capacity amid repairs to a reactor feed pump.

Boston Edison Co's 670 MW Pilgrim nuclear station in Plymouth, Mass., was scheduled to resume operation Saturday after being idled last week because of a saltwater leak in a set of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
Niagara Mohawk Power Corp will shut the 1,120 MW Nine MIle Point Two nuclear plant in Scriba on Saturday for a five-week refueling program.

In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), non-firm electricity for heavy demand hours on Friday in the western portion of the state was assessed at $19.00-$20.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Wednesday's quote.
According to market sources, next-day power in eastern NYPP was valued at $22.00-$23.00, also flat from Wednesday.
Off-peak NYPP electricity for Friday was again discussed near $15.00 per MWh.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), next-day power trading was thin with buyers on the sideline awaiting a price decline, but suppliers were reluctant to sell below current levels, traders said.
Offers for peak, non-firm electricity for Friday were assessed in the $28.00-$30.00 range, but bids were in the $24.00-$26.00 level.
The latest forecasts indicated the temperatures in the Northeast would turn higher-than-normal next week.
